```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(plyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(lsr)
exp1_dat <- read.csv("exp1_data.csv")
exp2_dat <- read.csv("exp2_data.csv")
```
# Summary
The data are available on the OSF (https://osf.io/3htpj/). The OSF repository for the original paper does not include the relevant code for the analysis or the modelling, though I was able to find the model code on GitHub after some searching (https://github.com/hayleydorfman/valence-control). Overall, I was unable to reproduce anything but figure 2a, and part of the result of the behavioural analyses reported for experiment 2. 

# Results
## Behavioural Analyses
### Experiment 1
```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

##Overall
dfov <- ddply(exp1_dat, c("subject","feedback"), summarise,
              intervention = mean(latent_guess))
overallT <- t.test(data = dfov, intervention ~ feedback, paired = TRUE)
overallE <- cohensD(intervention ~ feedback, data = dfov, method = "paired")

##Conditions
df1 <- ddply(exp1_dat, c("subject","condition","feedback"), summarise,
             intervention = mean(latent_guess))
#Adversarial
adv <- df1 %>% filter(condition == 1)
advT <- t.test(data = adv, intervention ~ feedback, paired = TRUE)
advE <- cohensD(intervention ~ feedback, data = adv, method = "paired")
  
#Benevolent
benv <- df1 %>% filter(condition == 2)
benvT <- t.test(data = benv, intervention ~ feedback, paired = TRUE)
benvE <- cohensD(intervention ~ feedback, data = benv, method = "paired")
  
#Neutral
neut <- df1 %>% filter(condition == 3)
neutT <- t.test(data = neut, intervention ~ feedback, paired = TRUE)
neutE <- cohensD(intervention ~ feedback, data = neut, method = "paired")
```
#### Results reported:
"As a preliminary manipulation check, we verified that participants’ beliefs about hidden causes varied with the outcome valence in a conditionspecific manner (Fig. 2a). Participants were more likely to believe that a hidden cause resulted in negative outcomes, as opposed to positive outcomes, overall, t(71) = 16.82, p < .0001, d = -0.32, 95% confidence interval, or CI = [-0.55, -0.08]. Importantly, participants were more likely to believe that the hidden agent had intervened after negative than after positive outcomes in the adversarial condition, t(71) = 66.24, p < .0001, d = -0.28, 95% CI = [-0.51, -0.04], and after positive than after negative outcomes in the benevolent condition, t(71) = -71.35, p < .0001, d = -0.99, 95% CI = [-1.23, -0.74]. Participants were also slightly more likely to believe that the hidden agent had intervened after negative outcomes in the neutral condition, t(71) = 6.83, p < .0001, d = -0.31, 95% CI = [-0.55, -0.08]. We will revisit this effect in the context of our computational model."

#### Results reproduced:
I must be missing something, as I was unable to reproduce these results at all:

"Participants were more likely to believe that a hidden cause resulted in negative outcomes, as opposed to positive outcomes, overall," t(`r overallT$parameter`) = `r overallT$statistic`, p = `r format(overallT$p.value, scientific=FALSE)`, d = `r overallE`, CI = [`r overallT$conf.int[1] `,`r overallT$conf.int[2]`]

"Importantly, participants were more likely to believe that the hidden agent had intervened after negative than after positive outcomes in the adversarial condition, " t(`r advT$parameter`) = `r advT$statistic`, p = `r format(advT$p.value, scientific=FALSE)`, d = `r advE`, CI = [`r advT$conf.int[1] `, `r advT$conf.int[2]`]

", and after positive than after negative outcomes in the benevolent condition," t(`r benvT$parameter`) = `r benvT$statistic`, p = `r format(benvT$p.value, scientific=FALSE)`, d = `r benvE`, CI = [`r benvT$conf.int[1] `, `r benvT$conf.int[2]`]

"Participants were also slightly more likely to believe that the hidden agent had intervened after negative outcomes in the neutral condition," t(`r neutT$parameter`) = `r neutT$statistic`, p = `r format(neutT$p.value, scientific=FALSE)`, d = `r neutE`, CI = [`r neutT$conf.int[1] `, `r neutT$conf.int[2]`]



Figure 2a was reproducible:
 
 
```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
df <- ddply(exp1_dat, c("condition","feedback"), summarise,
               N    = length(latent_guess),
               intervention = mean(latent_guess),
               sd   = sd(latent_guess),
               se   = sd / sqrt(N) )

ggplot(df, aes(x = condition, y = intervention, fill = factor(feedback))) + geom_bar(position="dodge",stat="identity")+ ylab("Intervention Probability") + xlab("") + ylim(0,1)+ geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=intervention-se, ymax=intervention+se), width=.1, position=position_dodge(.9))


```

#### Issues
I was unable to reproduce anything but figure 2a (and the degrees of freedom for the t-tests).

### Experiment 2
```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
exp2_dat <- read.csv("exp2_data.csv")#overall

##Overall
dfov2 <- ddply(exp2_dat, c("subject","feedback"), summarise,
              intervention = mean(latent_guess))
overallT2 <- t.test(data = dfov2, intervention ~ feedback, paired = TRUE)
overallE2 <- cohensD(intervention ~ feedback, data = dfov2, method = "paired")

#C#onditions
df2 <- ddply(exp2_dat, c("subject","condition","feedback"), summarise,
             intervention = mean(latent_guess))
#Adversarial
adv2 <- df2 %>% filter(condition == 1)
advT2 <- t.test(data = adv2, intervention ~ feedback, paired = TRUE)
advE2 <- cohensD(intervention ~ feedback, data = adv2, method = "paired")

#Benevolent
benv2 <- df1 %>% filter(condition == 2)
benvT2 <- t.test(data = benv2, intervention ~ feedback, paired = TRUE)
benvE2 <- cohensD(intervention ~ feedback, data = benv2, method = "paired")

#Neutral
neut2 <- df1 %>% filter(condition == 3)
neutT2 <- t.test(data = neut2, intervention ~ feedback, paired = TRUE)
neutE2 <- cohensD(intervention ~ feedback, data = neut2, method = "paired")

```

#### Results reported:
"Results of Experiment 2 replicated those of Experiment 1: Participants believed that the hidden agent caused negative outcomes more often than positive outcomes across all conditions, t(254) = 6.26, p < .0001, d = -0.06, 95% CI = [-0.18, 0.06], and there was a significant difference between belief in the hidden agent for good outcomes in the benevolent and neutral conditions and for bad outcomes in the adversarial and neutral conditions, t(254) = 7.03, p < .0001, d = 0.29, 95% CI = [0.17, 0.41]."

#### Results reproduced:
"Results of Experiment 2 replicated those of Experiment 1: Participants believed that the hidden agent caused negative outcomes more often than positive outcomes across all conditions," t(`r overallT2$parameter`) = `r overallT2$statistic`, p = `r format(overallT2$p.value, scientific=FALSE)`, d = `r overallE2`, CI = [`r overallT2$conf.int[1] `,`r overallT2$conf.int[2]`]

"and there was a significant difference between belief in the hidden agent for good outcomes in the benevolent and neutral conditions and for bad outcomes in the adversarial and neutral conditions," // I do not know what analysis the paper reported here, as it is only one result where in experiment 1 there were three (one each for adversarial, benevolent, and neutral). I did a paired t-test for each condition, as in experiment 1, but none of the results matched the result reported at this point in the paper.

#### Issues:
The result of the ``overall'' t-test was reproducible, except for the effect size and confidence interval. It is unclear what the second reported t-test represents, and I was unable to reproduce this.

## Computational Modeling 
The code for the computational modelling is not available on the OSF. I did, however, find the relevant Matlab code on GitHub (https://github.com/hayleydorfman/valence-control). While I have access to Matlab, I do not have much experience with Matlab, so my inability to run this code doesn't necessarily mean much. Unless I am really misunderstanding something, the code provided on GitHub is missing at least the likelihood function "lik_asym". 

# Conclusion
Overall, I was unable to reproduce anything but figure 2a, and part of the result of the behavioural analyses reported for experiment 2. I was entirely unable to run the model code, as there seemed to be functions missing (though my Matlab skills are very limited, so I was unable to try to adjust anything to potentially make it work). I tried to reproduce the behavioural results reported in the paper, and failed to reproduce anything but figure 2a and part of the result of the behavioural analyses reported for experiment 2. I am unsure whether I made a mistake while trying to reproduce the results without the relevant code, or whether the authors did not report all the information needed for me to successfully do so, or if there may be a mistake in the original analysis code, or if there is yet another possible explanation.
